questions.q: Why does the storefront's MySQL application connect through storefront_app@'10.20.%' with a scoped role, rather than as root?
options: Roles are required before any GRANT statement will run
It improves query performance compared to connecting as root
MySQL 8 no longer allows the root account to connect remotely under any circumstances
Least privilege — the account should only be able to reach the storefront schema from the expected host range
questions.explain: This is the least-privilege principle: an application account should only have the access and reach it actually needs.

questions.q: Why is RMAN, not just Data Pump, used for FINPRD's regular backup schedule?
options: RMAN is faster for every workload regardless of size
Data Pump has been deprecated in current Oracle versions
RMAN performs block-level physical backups and supports incrementals against a database in ARCHIVELOG mode, which Data Pump's logical export/import doesn't provide
Data Pump can only export the SYSTEM tablespace
questions.explain: RMAN is the physical, block-level backup tool built for full/incremental schedules and point-in-time recovery; Data Pump is a logical export/import tool used more for migrations or one-off exports.

questions.q: Why does the storefront need Percona XtraBackup and binary logs in addition to nightly mysqldump?
options: XtraBackup replaces the need for any user accounts
Binary logs are only used for replication, never backup
mysqldump cannot back up the customers table
A logical dump alone means losing up to a day of orders if the server fails mid-afternoon; XtraBackup plus binlogs support recovery to the minute of failure
questions.explain: A nightly-only logical backup leaves a recovery point objective gap; physical backup plus binary logs enable point-in-time recovery closer to the moment of failure.

questions.q: Why does the nightly ETL job get its own reporting_app role on PostgreSQL instead of using the bi_readonly role?
options: bi_readonly is reserved exclusively for human users, never automated jobs
PostgreSQL doesn't allow the same role to be used by two different processes
ETL jobs must always run as the postgres superuser
bi_readonly only has SELECT access, but the ETL job needs to INSERT/UPDATE sales_fact, so it needs a narrower role scoped to that specific write access
questions.explain: Least privilege means giving the ETL job exactly the write access it needs on sales_fact, not the broad read-only grant meant for BI analysts.

questions.q: What PostgreSQL backup approach supports point-in-time recovery for the analytics database, beyond a plain pg_dump?
options: pg_basebackup combined with WAL archiving
pg_dumpall run twice a day
Increasing shared_buffers
CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements
questions.explain: pg_basebackup provides a physical base backup, and continuous WAL archiving on top of it is what enables point-in-time recovery — pg_dump alone is a point-in-time logical snapshot only.
